predicate.name: Is canonical regime
predicate.description: Marks a Regime as canonical; every declared Regime satisfies it.

predicate.name: Requirement satisfied
predicate.description: Minimal requirement-satisfaction predicate used by the theory interface.

predicate.name: Profile well formed
predicate.description: A regime profile is well formed when its regime is canonical.

predicate.name: Under split pressure
predicate.description: Holds when the canonical axes record a split-forcing transformation.

predicate.name: Regime application admissible
predicate.description: A regime application is admissible when the substrate element is neutral relative to the consequence system and framework.

predicate.name: Non-collapsing
predicate.description: Two regimes are non-collapsing when some transformation receives different classification values.

predicate.name: Graph well formed
predicate.description: Every vertex in the graph carries a canonical regime.

predicate.name: Field changes
predicate.description: A field takes different values at two presentations.

predicate.name: Minimal support
predicate.description: Every supported field is relevant: two presentations that differ only in that field have different invariants.

predicate.name: Effective instance
predicate.description: An admissible step that changes at least one field.

predicate.name: Applicable
predicate.description: A family has an effective instance somewhere in the presentation space, independent of any finite domain.

predicate.name: Has verdict
predicate.description: A verdict is the derived verdict of a family relative to an invariant basis.

predicate.name: Step relation
predicate.description: Steps inside a domain whose endpoints have equal invariants.

predicate.name: Step identity
predicate.description: The identity relation generated by the invariant-preserving steps inside a domain.

predicate.name: Step collapse
predicate.description: Two bases generate the same identity relation on a domain.

predicate.name: Step agreement
predicate.description: Every step inside a domain is preserved by both bases or changed by both.
